name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Deliver: Push link coverage toward 100% at +5%/day (the access gate)

name: Reel
text:
Do this: Run a weekly manual audit of the 20% of links that drive 80% of traffic. Flag dead links and redirects in a shared sheet. Fix only the ones that break user flows—ignore cosmetic or low-traffic ones.

Trade-off: We accept slower full coverage to hit the +5%/day gate faster. Manual triage is slower than automation but guarantees we don’t waste time on noise while still pushing the critical links over the finish line.

name: Scriv
text: Manual audits won’t scale—traffic shifts weekly, so yesterday’s "top 20%" is today’s noise. Worse, we’ll waste time fixing links that break nothing while missing new dead ones in the long tail. Simpler: automate a weekly scan of *all* links, rank by traffic impact, and auto-flag only those that break user flows. Settle it with a 24-hour spike: build the scraper, run it on a sample, and compare its false-positive rate to the manual sheet.

name: Chisel
text:
Automate a weekly scan of every link, rank by traffic impact, and auto-flag only those that break user flows. This cuts manual work to near-zero while catching new dead links faster than a manual top-20% audit ever could. The trade-off: we accept some false positives (harmless redirects or cosmetic breaks) to keep the gate moving at +5%/day.

name: Sift
text: The real risk isn’t false positives—it’s the hidden cost of automating a system that assumes traffic patterns are static. If a new high-traffic link appears mid-week, your weekly scan will miss it until the next run, while a manual top-20% audit catches it immediately. Settle it by running both: automate a daily scan of *all* links, but pair it with a 10-minute manual check of the top 20% traffic shifts *since the last scan*. That’s the only way to guarantee +5%/day without gambling on stale data.

name: Scope
text: Run both: weekly manual audits of the top 20% traffic links *and* automated weekly scans of all links. Manual audits catch sudden traffic spikes immediately; automation handles the long tail without extra labor. Trade-off: we accept some overlap and extra upkeep to guarantee no dead link slips through the gate. This keeps the +5%/day climb steady while minimizing user-facing breaks.

name: Scriv
text: Scriv: The real risk isn’t overlap—it’s that running both systems doubles the work without solving the core problem: traffic shifts daily, not weekly. The better alternative is to automate a *daily* scan of all links, rank by real-time traffic impact, and auto-flag only those breaking user flows. Settle it by running a 48-hour pilot: compare the daily scan’s false positives against the manual top-20% audit’s misses. If the daily scan catches more critical breaks with fewer false positives, kill the manual audit.

name: Echo
text:
DECISION: Run a daily automated scan of all links, rank by real-time traffic impact, and auto-flag only those breaking user flows—manual audits are dropped.

Result: A system that catches dead links faster than weekly checks, with near-zero manual work. Owner: Me.
